metadata.condition_name: Sporadic hemiplegic migraine with reversible MRI changes and focal motor seizures
metadata.difficulty_description: Moderate difficulty due to MRI showing diffuse cortical swelling and T2/FLAIR hyperintensity (concerning for ischemia or encephalitis) with simultaneously normal DWI. Focal motor seizures complicate the picture (migralepsy consideration). Sporadic hemiplegic migraine diagnosis requires systematic exclusion of acute infarction, MELAS, epilepsy, and autoimmune causes.

patient.presenting_complaint: Left-sided throbbing headache with right arm weakness, speech difficulty, and a witnessed shaking episode
patient.hpi: A 26-year-old woman presented to the emergency department brought by her partner with a 3-hour history of severe left-sided throbbing headache that began approximately 30 minutes after she developed blurred vision in her right visual field. Shortly after the headache peaked, her partner noticed that she was struggling to find words and her right arm appeared weak. Within the following hour she experienced two brief episodes of right-hand rhythmic jerking lasting approximately 90 seconds each, during which she was unresponsive, followed by postictal confusion lasting approximately 20 minutes. She has had episodes of unilateral throbbing headache accompanied by transient arm weakness affecting alternating sides since the age of 14. During those earlier attacks, the weakness has always resolved completely within a few hours, and previous assessments including head CT, brain MRI, MR angiography, lumbar puncture, and basic metabolic and mitochondrial blood tests were all documented as normal at age 17 and again at age 22. She was commenced on topiramate 75 mg twice daily approximately two years ago following inadequate response to flunarizine; despite this she continues to have one to two attacks monthly. There is no family history of similar episodes, hemiplegic migraine, or any neurological condition. She does not smoke, drinks alcohol only occasionally, and uses no illicit substances. She takes topiramate and a combined oral contraceptive pill (Mercilon, desogestrel 150 mcg / ethinylestradiol 20 mcg). She has no known drug allergies.
pmh: Sporadic hemiplegic migraine — diagnosed age 22, ICHD-3 1.2.3

medications.indication: Contraception — WHO Category 4 — must be stopped

family_history: No family history of hemiplegic migraine, stroke, or neurological disease. Mother has tension-type headache.

social_history.note: Non-smoker, occasional alcohol (1-2 units/week), no illicit drugs. Lives with partner. Works as teaching assistant. Not pregnant.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, mildly confused, oriented to person and place but not time. Motor aphasia — single word responses, no paraphasic errors. Follows simple one-step commands.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Visual fields by confrontation: mild right homonymous visual field restriction that patient reports is improving from earlier. Pupils 4mm equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full. Fundoscopy normal. Facial symmetry slightly reduced on right with right lower facial droop. Tongue protruded midline.
neurological_exam.motor: Right upper extremity: power 3/5 throughout. Right lower extremity: power 4/5. Left upper and lower extremity: power 5/5. Tone normal bilaterally.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Brisk throughout. Right plantar extensor (Babinski positive). Left plantar flexor.
neurological_exam.sensation: Intact to light touch and pinprick bilaterally. No cortical sensory deficits.
neurological_exam.coordination: Limited on right due to weakness. Left cerebellar tests intact.
neurological_exam.gait: Not assessed — patient was bed-bound at presentation.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch and pinprick bilaterally. No cortical sensory deficits.

red_herrings.finding: Two focal right-sided motor seizures during the attack
red_herrings.misleading_diagnosis: New-onset epilepsy / Todd's palsy explaining the hemiparesis
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Seizures are migralepsy — focal seizures triggered by hemiplegic migraine aura, not a primary epileptic disorder. EEG showed no epileptiform discharges or hemispheric dysfunction. The MRI abnormalities (cortical swelling, FLAIR signal) are reversible and DWI-negative, inconsistent with post-ictal changes from status epilepticus.

red_herrings.finding: Diffuse left hemispheric cortical swelling and T2/FLAIR hyperintensity
red_herrings.misleading_diagnosis: Autoimmune encephalitis (NMDAR or other) or HSV encephalitis
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Critically, DWI is normal, CSF shows no pleocytosis, autoimmune antibody panels negative, HSV PCR negative. Reversibility on 72-hour follow-up MRI confirms CSD-mediated cortical hyperaemia in hemiplegic migraine.

red_herrings.finding: Current use of combined OCP (Mercilon EE 20 mcg)
red_herrings.misleading_diagnosis: OCP-related cerebral venous thrombosis or ischaemic event
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: MRV would show no sinus thrombosis. DWI is normal excluding arterial infarction. However, OCP is WHO Category 4 in hemiplegic migraine and must be stopped, even though it is not the cause of this acute attack — this is a critical management action the agent must identify.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Sporadic hemiplegic migraine (ICHD-3 1.2.3) with migralepsy and reversible MRI changes

differential.key_features: Excluded by normal DWI/ADC. MRA normal. No vascular occlusion. 12-year history of identical reversible episodes.
Excluded by normal CSF (no pleocytosis), negative autoimmune panel, negative HSV PCR, and full reversibility on follow-up MRI.
EEG showed no epileptiform discharges or hemispheric dysfunction. Seizures explained as migralepsy (triggered by hemiplegic aura). 12-year history of episodes without primary seizure diagnosis.
Excluded by normal serum and CSF lactate, normal pyruvate, and negative mtDNA heteroplasmy testing. No maternal inheritance history.
Normal MRA/MRV, negative antiphospholipid antibodies, DWI negative. Though OCP use is a risk factor, no imaging evidence of thrombosis.

optimal_actions.action: Perform urgent MRI brain with DWI, FLAIR, T1+Gd, and MRA to exclude acute infarction and vascular cause
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Diffuse left cortical swelling and FLAIR hyperintensity but normal DWI — excludes acute infarction. Normal MRA.

optimal_actions.action: Perform EEG to evaluate for primary epileptic disorder versus migralepsy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Mild post-ictal slowing, no epileptiform discharges, no hemispheric dysfunction — argues against primary epilepsy as the underlying cause

tool_parameters.indication: seizures with hemiparesis — exclude status epilepticus and epileptic cause

optimal_actions.action: Send comprehensive bloods including CBC, metabolic panel, inflammatory markers, serum lactate, thyroid function, and autoimmune/antiphospholipid screen
optimal_actions.expected_finding: All normal — excludes metabolic, mitochondrial, and autoimmune causes. Normal lactate argues against MELAS.

optimal_actions.action: Perform lumbar puncture to analyse CSF including lactate, glucose, protein, cell count, oligoclonal bands, HSV PCR, and VZV PCR
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Normal CSF — no pleocytosis, normal lactate, negative HSV/VZV PCR. Excludes viral encephalitis and MELAS.

optimal_actions.action: Arrange repeat MRI brain at 72 hours to confirm reversibility of cortical changes
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Near-complete resolution of cortical swelling and FLAIR signal — confirming reversible CSD-mediated changes consistent with hemiplegic migraine

optimal_actions.action: Stop combined oral contraceptive pill (Mercilon) immediately — WHO MEC Category 4 absolute contraindication in hemiplegic migraine
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Combined OCP is WHO Category 4 in hemiplegic migraine — unacceptable stroke risk. Must stop immediately and switch to progesterone-only pill or implant.

optimal_actions.action: Consider optimising migraine prevention — current topiramate dose may be inadequate given 1-2 attacks/month. Discuss adding sodium valproate or switching to verapamil (valproate requires pregnancy prevention discussion).
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Preventive therapy rationalisation — flunarizine failed, topiramate sub-optimal. Consider verapamil 240 mg SR or valproate 400-600 mg (with contraception plan).

optimal_actions.action: Prescribe progesterone-only contraception to replace OCP — desogestrel 75 mcg (Cerazette) daily or Nexplanon implant
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Safe contraception for patient with hemiplegic migraine — progesterone-only preparations are WHO MEC Category 1

critical_actions: Normal DWI must be recognised as excluding acute infarction despite alarming FLAIR/cortical swelling findings
Stop combined oral contraceptive pill (WHO MEC Category 4) and prescribe progesterone-only alternative
Confirm reversibility of MRI changes at 72-hour follow-up
Migralepsy must be recognised — seizures triggered by hemiplegic aura, not primary epilepsy
contraindicated_actions: Continue combined OCP in any migraine with aura including hemiplegic subtype (WHO Category 4)
Prescribe triptans for hemiplegic migraine during acute attack (contraindicated by ICHD and BNF)
Prescribe ergotamine for acute hemiplegic migraine attack (contraindicated)
Commence anticoagulation (warfarin, DOAC) without MRV evidence of cerebral venous thrombosis
Commence anti-seizure medication for migralepsy in the absence of true primary epilepsy diagnosis
key_reasoning_points: Normal DWI despite dramatic FLAIR changes and cortical swelling is the pathognomonic pattern of hemiplegic migraine — CSD causes cortical hyperaemia and oedema without ischaemia.

Focal motor seizures in the setting of hemiplegic migraine constitute migralepsy (ICHD-3 1.4.3) — seizures triggered by the migraine aura. EEG not showing interictal epileptiform discharges supports this distinction from primary epilepsy.
Absence of family history in any of the three known HM genes supports sporadic hemiplegic migraine — this is the correct diagnosis even with normal genetic panel.

Combined OCP is WHO MEC Category 4 (absolute contraindication) in ALL migraine with aura including hemiplegic subtypes, even at the lowest oestrogen dose (EE 20 mcg). The attending must recognise and act on this at first contact.
12-year history of identical reversible episodes with prior normal investigations provides strong prior probability for the same mechanism. The agent should weight this history heavily.
CSF lactate normal and mtDNA heteroplasmy testing negative definitively excludes MELAS, which can produce identical reversible cortical changes in young women.

Full reversibility at 72-hour MRI is both diagnostically reassuring and clinically important — it differentiates hemiplegic migraine from autoimmune encephalitis (which shows persistence or progression).

signal_characteristics.FLAIR: gyral cortical hyperintensity with sulcal effacement

findings.mass_effect: mild sulcal effacement left hemisphere — consistent with vasogenic oedema
findings.borders: diffuse, non-territorial, no vascular territory demarcation

findings.location: circle of Willis and major cerebral arteries

signal_characteristics.MRA: patent bilateral ICA, MCA, ACA, PCA, basilar; no occlusion, stenosis, or dissection; no arterial filling defect

mri.impression: 1. Diffuse left hemispheric cortical swelling with T2/FLAIR gyral cortical hyperintensity and mild sulcal effacement. 2. Critically, DWI is NORMAL — no restricted diffusion, no cytotoxic oedema. No leptomeningeal or cortical enhancement. 3. Normal MRA — no arterial occlusion, stenosis, or dissection. The pattern of vasogenic cortical oedema without cytotoxic oedema and non-territorial distribution does not conform to an arterial infarct. Imaging differential includes cortical spreading depression, autoimmune encephalitis, and other causes of cortical vasogenic oedema. Follow-up MRI is recommended to assess reversibility. Clinical correlation recommended.

background.pdr: 6-7 Hz theta-range activity bilaterally — post-ictal slowing
background.overall: mild diffuse slowing consistent with post-ictal state; no hemispheric asymmetry

findings.morphology: Mild diffuse slowing, predominantly theta range (5-7 Hz) consistent with postictal state. No epileptiform discharges.
Comparable mild background slowing. No focal hemispheric asymmetry greater than left.
No persistent hemispheric dysfunction. No delta-wave asymmetry. No ictal activity. No sharp waves, spike-and-wave, or epileptiform discharges recorded during this session.

eeg.impression: This is an ABNORMAL EEG. Mild diffuse background slowing in the theta range bilaterally, consistent with a post-ictal or encephalopathic state. No interictal epileptiform discharges. No ictal activity or electrographic seizures recorded. No persistent hemispheric asymmetry. Clinical correlation recommended.

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 15 cmH2O. Protein: 0.36 g/L. Glucose: 3.8 mmol/L.

signal_characteristics.FLAIR: marked interval improvement; residual mild cortical signal change only

signal_characteristics.MRA: patent; no change from initial scan

output.impression: Marked interval improvement compared with prior study. Near-complete resolution of left hemispheric cortical swelling and FLAIR signal changes. Sulcal pattern restored. DWI normal throughout — no restricted diffusion. MRA unchanged and patent. The imaging changes were reversible over 72 hours. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Patent circle of Willis. No stenosis, occlusion, dissection, or aneurysm.
Patent bilateral internal and external carotid arteries. No dissection. No significant stenosis.

output.impression: Normal MRA head and neck. No stenosis, occlusion, dissection, or aneurysm identified.

output.proposed: combined oral contraceptive (ethinylestradiol 20 mcg + desogestrel) in hemiplegic migraine with motor aura
contraindications: Combined OCP is WHO MEC Category 4 (absolute contraindication) in ALL migraine with aura including hemiplegic subtypes — unacceptable ischaemic stroke risk due to oestrogen-mediated procoagulant state combined with CSD haemodynamic vulnerability
Risk applies to all doses of oestrogen including EE 20 mcg (low-dose) — dose does not mitigate Category 4 classification in hemiplegic migraine
warnings: Combined OCP should not be continued in migraine with aura; progestin-only alternatives (desogestrel 75 mcg, etonogestrel implant) are WHO MEC Category 1 in migraine with aura and are appropriate replacements
No oestrogen-containing preparation is appropriate in any subtype of migraine with aura
alternatives: desogestrel 75 mcg (Cerazette) — progesterone-only pill, WHO MEC Category 1

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.

ct.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No haemorrhage, mass, hydrocephalus, or large-territory infarct.

findings: Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.
No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

specialized_test.impression: Study within normal limits. No abnormality identified; non-contributory.
